A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDSMC/D3SMC research by the same authors. Their readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from Appendix F to G.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian-mixture experiments, FFHQ restoration measurements, and qualitative binary-MNIST denoising results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds protein structure completion experiments, computational ablations, and expanded image-restoration measurements.

M1.justification: The core DDSMC and D3SMC procedures are retained. Appendix F newly adapts DDSMC to Chroma's correlated-noise protein prior through whitening, an SVD transformation, and coordinate-dependent observation noise, providing a bounded extension of the inference procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains Gaussian mixtures, FFHQ restoration, and binary MNIST, while adding backbone structure completion for five PDB proteins. Section 5.3 and Appendix G.3 introduce a biological domain with varying observation sparsity and noise conditions.

E2.justification: ADP-3D is added as an evaluated protein-completion comparator in Figures 4 and 15. The existing GMM and FFHQ comparator sets are retained; the additional DDRM step-count variants change settings rather than comparator identity.

E3.justification: FFHQ evaluation increases from 100 to 1,000 images and adds PSNR. New experiments vary particle counts, ODE steps, and DDRM sampling budgets; protein evaluation uses RMSD with 200 DDSMC versus 1,000 ADP-3D steps. The printed FFHQ time/noise schedules also change from v1 Equations 67–68 to v2 Equations 79–80, without establishing whether those corrections reflect changed implementations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained reconstruction-function and decoupling ablations, v2 tests single-particle DDSMC against DAPS, allocation of score-evaluation budgets between particles and ODE steps, and DDRM step sensitivity (Tables 4–8 and 9–10). Protein experiments additionally examine sensitivity to noise, observation sparsity, and particle count.

E5.justification: The GMM reporting of 20 seeds and 95% CLT intervals is retained. V2 newly reports image-level standard deviations for FFHQ LPIPS and PSNR across 1,000 images. Protein experiments report eight seeds and display shaded bands, although the bands' precise statistical definition is not stated.

E6.justification: GMM Tables 1–2 retain their numerical values, but v2 adds substantial particle/step results, FFHQ PSNR scores, and protein RMSD curves. FFHQ Table 3 contains revised averages under the expanded evaluation, such as MCGDiff middle-inpainting LPIPS changing from 0.12 to 0.10; this is not evidence of a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The original marginal-equality proof is retained, with its forward/backward inversion assumption made explicit in Remark A.2. V2 corrects the VP proposal covariance (v1 Equation 54 versus v2 Equation 57) and DDIM coefficient (66 versus 78), and derives the protein whitening transformation. Proposition 3.1 mainly formalizes the existing SMC consistency argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the claimed empirical applicability to protein structure completion. The central contributions—generalized decoupling, asymptotically exact SMC, and the discrete extension—remain.

C2.justification: Remark 3.2 explicitly distinguishes consistency for the chosen prior from equality with the standard diffusion prior, materially qualifying the interpretation of exactness. New discussion attributes the improvement over DAPS to the SMC component and explains particle-versus-ODE budget tradeoffs, including why score-evaluation counts need not track runtime under parallelization (Appendix G.1.3–G.1.5).

D1.justification: V2 adds a DDSMC code-access link, explicit FFHQ downsampling information, and image attribution details. It also documents Chroma weight access and protein implementation settings, including noise-dependent ADP-3D learning rates and sampling budgets, and expands the explanation of ODE execution and computational cost.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gibbs-sampling references by Coeurdoux et al. and Wu et al., an SMC foundation reference, and protein-related work including ADP-3D, Chroma, and PDB sources. The established positioning relative to DAPS, TDS, and MCGDiff remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. V2 locally rewrites the PF-ODE and SMC explanations, adds protein and computational-analysis subsections plus an Impact Statement, and reorganizes the experimental appendix around the new protein appendix.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ICML layout with running headers, revised typography and table styling, and extensive reflow of existing displays. It adds Tables 4–11 and protein Figures 4 and 15. Earlier qualitative figures are retained but relocated, renumbered, or resized, with FFHQ captions expanded to identify image sources.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence through single-particle and matched-score-budget controls, addressing v1's limited analysis of computational tradeoffs and the contribution of SMC. Corrected equations and explicit qualification of the target prior improve technical clarity. Expanded FFHQ reporting, protein experiments, and code-access information strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. Real-data reconstruction metrics still do not establish posterior fidelity, but the central claims are substantially better supported and easier to assess.
